title_original: UK-Ireland box office preview: A24’s ‘You Can See Everything’ gets widest ever release for a non-music doc
excerpt_original: Lionsgate’s latest ‘Hunger Games’ film opens in 660 cinemas.

blocks.alt: 'You Can See everything', 'the hunger games: sunrise on the reaping'

blocks.text: Source: A24 / Lionsgate
‘You Can See everything’, ‘the hunger games: sunrise on the reaping’

Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping is the biggest new release in UK and Ireland cinemas this weekend as A24’s You Can See Everything gets the widest ever opening for a non-music documentary.

Sunrise On The Reaping is out in 660 locations and is the widest opening for The Hunger Games films as well as Lionsgate’s second-widest opening of all time. The film made nearly £2m in previews on Wednesday (November 18).

It marks the sixth entry in The Hunger Games franchise, which is based on the young adult novels by Suzanne Collins. The highest-grossing was 2013’s Catching Fire with a £12.2m debut and £34.2m cume while the lowest-grossing was its most recent instalment, 2023’s The Ballad Of Songbirds And Snakes , which opened on £5.4m and finished at £18.2m.

Francis Lawrence returns to direct Sunrise On The Reaping , having directed all but one of the previous entries. The new film is set 24 years before the original trilogy and centres on the 50 th games. The cast is led by Mckenna Grace, Joseph Zada, Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, Glenn Close and Kieran Culkin with appearances from original stars Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson.

A24’s eagerly anticipated Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything finally launches in the UK in around 590 venues, with Holdover handling distribution on its behalf. This makes it the widest ever opening for a non-music documentary, ahead of Ocean With David Attenborough which debuted in 531 venues last year.

That title opened on £577,000 for a cume of £1.7m but the highest-grossing non-music documentary in the UK and Ireland is Michael Moore’s 2003 film Fahrenheit 9/11 which grossed £6.5m after opening on £1.3m.

Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s film will be hoping to at least match that thanks to an unprecedented level of word of mouth since opening in North America last month, where it has already grossed $90m. Many screenings over the weekend are already sold out, with venues continuing to be added, and excitement particularly strong among Gen Z and under-35s.

You Can See Everything follows Holmes, who was convicted of fraud over her health technology company Theranos, in the days leading up to her 11-year prison sentence. It first premiered at Telluride as a surprise screening before going on to New York Film Festival.
Helen Mirren, Your Mother and Sundance winner

In event cinema, Trafalgar Releasing has screenings of theatre production Giant , starring John Lithgow as Roald Dahl, in 462 locations and live concert BTS World Tour ‘Arirang’ In Kaohsiung in 200. Vue Lumiere has Cbeebies Panto 2026: Treasure Island in 381 locations.

Helen Mirren stars in A Talent For Murder which Universal is opening in 353 venues. Anton Corbijn’s film follows a junior literary editor who travels to Switzerland to try and persuade acclaimed novelist Patricia Highsmith to write another instalment of the Ripley books. Alden Ehrenreich and Olivia Cooke also star.

blocks.alt: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother

blocks.text: Source: Toronto Film Festival
‘Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’

Amazon MGM has Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother in 215 cinemas. Mahershala Ali stars in Bassim Tariq’s thriller, which first premiered in Toronto, as a devoutly religious hitman and recent widower navigating grief, family and survival. Further cast include John Cho, Giancarlo Esposito and Tramell Tilmman.

blocks.text: Park Circus is re-releasing the 2011 animation Arthur Christmas in 151 locations.

Curzon is launching Sundance award-winner Josephine in 52 sites. Beth de Araujo’s film centres on an eight-year-old girl who witnesses a sexual assault. It won the grand jury prize and the audience award in Sundance before going on to screen at Berlinale and BFI London. Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan star.

Poh Si Teng’s war documentary American Doctor opens in 11 cinemas for Conic Film. The Sundance premiere follows three American doctors – Palestinian, Jewish and Zoroastrian – who travel to Gaza to provide medical aid.

BFI Distribution is releasing dark comedy Filipiñana in six venues. Rafael Manuel’s debut follows a 17-year-old girl working as a “tee-girl” at a posh golf resort in the Philippines. It won the special jury award for creative vision at Sundance and is also the country’s entry for best international feature at the Oscars.

Further releases include animated Cinderella reimagining Steps via Netflix; Belgian-set drama Heysel 85 via Icon Film Distribution; football documentary The Match via Disney; and Indian films Sathyavan Savithri and 70 Syaal via Zee Studios.
